study: Batched support-identity mapping in optional local GCN search
change: Map equal-size proposal supports in one tensor batch, retain batch membership and sorted-unique checks, and cache local endpoint identities. Full-graph acceptance is unchanged.
verification: 88 unit tests passed, including exact CPU/CUDA agreement between individual and batch key mapping and rejection of invalid support batches. Both paired search runs passed full-graph non-regression checks and source-hash verification.
prior_results: local_search_initial_context.json and its raw reports are preserved. Previous paired full/local ratios were approximately 0.895 and 1.213. The new runs use the same input query/support files, but were executed at different times on a shared device.
cross_run_caution: On Cora, 115 of 120 local and 116 of 120 unchanged full-path final supports match their corresponding prior-run supports. Thus cross-run support changes cannot all be attributed to the mapping optimization. Floating-point-sensitive search is not assumed bitwise deterministic.
scope: Complete ungrouped single-edge refinement call, including region construction, gradients, local screening and full-graph acceptance. Excludes shared saliency initialization, candidate extraction, spectral preprocessing, model loading and final metric reporting.
limitations: Only two graph/seed combinations and twenty validation queries each; repeated timing pairs are not independent samples.
Local screening can change search trajectories and actual work. Equal binary metrics do not imply identical continuous metrics or supports.
The paired ratios do not establish a general end-to-end explanation speedup or any benefit of spectral coarsening.
The unchanged full-graph path remains the default; this optional path still requires broader validation.
decision: Retain the tested batching improvement in the optional local path. Do not keep tuning this small validation sample or promote it to the default based on these timings alone.
